It's freshly <radical>stamp</radical>ed with a number and due back at the end of the <radical>month</radical>. You put on the <kanji>clothing</kanji>, you obey the dress code, you admit out loud that you work there now. Under the fluorescent lights, every clerk ends up looking interchangeable in matching sleeves.
items.reading_mnemonic: The new clerk tugs at those balloon-stiff sleeves and mutters <reading>fook</reading> under his breath, disgusted at how they puff around his wrists. That same <reading>ふく</reading> gets grumbled every single shift.
items.description: 服 by itself almost always means clothing, as in everyday words for Western-style clothes or a uniform. The senses obey and admit only appear buried inside fixed multi-character compounds about submission or confession - standing alone, this character just means clothes.

items.reading_mnemonic: Downstream at the same crossing, the chef <reading>Han</reading> — the one who serves every dish split exactly in half — squats over the cracked plank and slices his lunch on it. He mutters 「<reading>はん</reading>」 with each cut: half for him, half for the current.

items.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk of <radical>grain</radical> on the left, beside it the <radical>small</radical> mark — one bristle off the very top, thinnest thing on the plant. Slice an hour the same way and the sliver left in your hand is one <kanji>second</kanji>.
items.reading_mnemonic: Byou is the hospital timekeeper with the stopwatch, and she counts out loud in a flat clipped bark — 「<reading>びょう</reading>」, びょう, びょう — one for every tick. She will not speed up and she will not stop. びょう is a single second landing.

items.meaning_mnemonic: See the whole character as a plate laid out to <radical>eat</radical> from: a heaping bowl of rice on the left, resting on a <radical>cliff</radical>-ledge. Crammed against it is a second helping some <radical>right hand</radical> snuck onto the tray before anyone could stop it. Two portions in one shape: the whole <kanji>meal</kanji>, seconds included.
items.reading_mnemonic: Han, the half-and-half chef, slices your whole dinner clean down the center before you can protest — that's just how he works here. You call out his name, <reading>Han</reading>, and he answers with a proud <reading>はん</reading>, holding up two identical plates like it settles the matter.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture 勉 as a sweatband wrung out mid-cram with sheer <radical>power</radical>, soaking the page underneath. items.meaning_mnemonic: On Sei's school field, the loudspeaker crackles out the final score and every <radical>mouth</radical> roars at once. The team's <radical>human legs</radical> carry them sprinting to the trophy stand, an <radical>altar</radical> of plastic and tape, to show it off overhead. Caps fly, the smallest kid gets hoisted onto shoulders, someone sprays a sports drink like champagne. The whole field erupts to <kanji>celebrate</kanji>.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Picture 泳 as one motion at the riverbank: an arm slices forward through the <radical>water</radical>. It flings a trail of <radical>drop</radical>lets out sideways behind it in one clean streak. That arm-cut trailing a spray of droplets is <kanji>swim</kanji> — caught mid-stroke, again and again.
items.reading_mnemonic: At the same riverbank, the lifeguard Ei blows her whistle every single stroke you take, shouting <reading>えい</reading>! — <reading>Ay</reading>! — like she's counting each one out loud. By the tenth lap her voice is the only thing keeping your arms moving.

items.meaning_mnemonic: On Sei's sports field, the archery club lines up their weapons, stacked curves of springy wood bent back on themselves, notched at both ends where the string bites in. A coach pulls one taut until it hums, holding a <radical>bow</radical> ready to fire.
items.reading_mnemonic: A boy named <reading>Kyu</reading> lines up his shot on the sports field, and the string gives a sharp <reading>きゅう</reading> as it snaps back into place, leaving nothing but that one clean sound behind.

items.meaning_mnemonic: Three droplets flick off the wet paintbrush and splash into the <radical>water</radical> below a hot spring. Flat layers of <radical>steam</radical> lie on the water, and the last wisp hooks up and peels into the cold — vapor rising off the pool.
items.reading_mnemonic: Kiki the tree spirit hides by the steaming pool and giggles at every gust. Cold spray hits her and she yelps <reading>き</reading>, sharp as a <reading>key</reading> turning in a lock, while the vapor drifts past her branch.
